## Purpose

Part of #60821. Complements #55380 (FlashInfer restore on SM75); this PR does not change backend selection.

On pre-SM80 GPUs (e.g. Turing/T4), FlashAttention is unavailable and FlashInfer is currently disabled on SM75, so auto-selection falls back to `TRITON_ATTN` or `FLEX_ATTENTION`. With current Triton these kernels don't use tensor cores on these GPUs, so prefill is much slower, and users get no indication why.

This PR:
- Logs a one-time warning in `CudaPlatform.get_attn_backend_cls` when a Triton-based backend is auto-selected on a GPU with compute capability < 8.0.
- Adds a note to `docs/design/attention_backends.md` (Automatic Selection).
- Adds unit tests in `tests/v1/attention/test_pre_sm80_backend_warning.py`.

The warning is not emitted when the user explicitly selects a backend, and it does not suggest switching backends, since no faster backend is currently available on SM75.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_pre_sm80_backend_warning.py -v` on a T4 (Google Colab)
- End-to-end: `LLM("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", dtype="half")` on a T4, checking the startup log
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files

## Test Result

Unit tests:
```

collected 6 items                                                              

tests/v1/attention/test_pre_sm80_backend_warning.py::test_warns_for_triton_backends_on_pre_sm80[AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN] PASSED [ 16%]
tests/v1/attention/test_pre_sm80_backend_warning.py::test_warns_for_triton_backends_on_pre_sm80[AttentionBackendEnum.FLEX_ATTENTION] PASSED [ 33%]
tests/v1/attention/test_pre_sm80_backend_warning.py::test_no_warning_otherwise[AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN-capability0] PASSED [ 50%]
tests/v1/attention/test_pre_sm80_backend_warning.py::test_no_warning_otherwise[AttentionBackendEnum.FLEX_ATTENTION-capability1] PASSED [ 66%]
tests/v1/attention/test_pre_sm80_backend_warning.py::test_no_warning_otherwise[AttentionBackendEnum.FLASHINFER-capability2] PASSED [ 83%]
tests/v1/attention/test_pre_sm80_backend_warning.py::test_no_warning_otherwise[AttentionBackendEnum.FLASH_ATTN-capability3] PASSED [100%]

============================== 6 passed in 2.64s ===============================
```

End-to-end on Tesla T4 (SM 7.5):
```
WARNING [cuda.py:199] Using the TRITON_ATTN attention backend on a GPU with compute capability 7.5 (pre-SM80, e.g. Turing/T4). On these GPUs the Triton attention kernels do not use tensor cores, so prefill can be much slower than on SM80+ GPUs. See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60821.
INFO [cuda.py:536] Using TRITON_ATTN attention backend out of potential backends: ['TRITON_ATTN', 'FLEX_ATTENTION'].
```

All pre-commit hooks pass.

Thanks for picking this up. #61015 covers item (2) of #60821, so I'll leave
that part to this PR. I tested it on a Tesla T4 (g4dn.2xlarge, main @
242e4213f with this PR's diff applied, which applied cleanly).
Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, `--dtype half`:

| case | selected backend | warning |
|---|---|---|
| auto-selection | TRITON_ATTN | fires once |
| explicit `TRITON_ATTN` | TRITON_ATTN | none |
| auto-selection + #55380's SM75 floor change | FLASHINFER | none |

`tests/v1/attention/test_pre_sm80_backend_warning.py`: 6 passed on the T4.

On the scope question (< 8.0 vs Turing-only), I think < 8.0 is right:
triton-lang/triton#5066 ("Deprecate MMAv1; fallback to FMA for
computeCapability < 80") applies to every arch below SM80, so V100 (SM70)
takes the same FMA path. I only verified SM75 myself (0 `mma.sync` in the
compiled `kernel_unified_attention` PTX), not V100.

The third row also shows the two PRs compose. Once #55380 lands, the
warning only fires where Triton is still auto-selected on SM75 (e.g.
head_size > 256, with the check I proposed on #55380), which is still
accurate there.

LGTM.

files.patch:
@@ -132,6 +132,14 @@ When no backend is specified (the default):
 4. If no backend is compatible, an error is raised listing all backends and
    their incompatibility reasons
 
+!!! note "Pre-SM80 GPUs (Turing, e.g. T4)"
+    FlashAttention requires SM80+, so on pre-SM80 GPUs automatic selection
+    usually falls back to a Triton-based backend (`TRITON_ATTN` or
+    `FLEX_ATTENTION`). With current Triton releases these kernels do not use
+    tensor cores on pre-SM80 GPUs, so prefill can be much slower than on
+    newer hardware. vLLM logs a one-time warning when this happens. See
+    [#60821](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60821) for status.
+
 ## Backend Priority (CUDA)
 
 When no backend is explicitly selected, vLLM chooses the first

@@ -0,0 +1,53 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Auto-selecting a Triton-based attention backend on a pre-SM80 GPU should
+emit a one-time performance warning.
+See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60821.
+"""
+
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.platforms.interface import DeviceCapability
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.registry import AttentionBackendEnum
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="CUDA-specific tests"
+)
+
+SM75 = DeviceCapability(major=7, minor=5)
+SM80 = DeviceCapability(major=8, minor=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "backend",
+    [AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN, AttentionBackendEnum.FLEX_ATTENTION],
+)
+def test_warns_for_triton_backends_on_pre_sm80(backend):
+    from vllm.platforms import cuda
+
+    with patch.object(cuda.logger, "warning_once") as warn:
+        cuda._warn_if_slow_pre_sm80_backend(backend, SM75)
+    warn.assert_called_once()
+    msg, *args = warn.call_args.args
+    assert "tensor cores" in msg
+    assert backend.name in args
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("backend", "capability"),
+    [
+        (AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN, SM80),
+        (AttentionBackendEnum.FLEX_ATTENTION, DeviceCapability(9, 0)),
+        (AttentionBackendEnum.FLASHINFER, SM75),
+        (AttentionBackendEnum.FLASH_ATTN, SM80),
+    ],
+)
+def test_no_warning_otherwise(backend, capability):
+    from vllm.platforms import cuda
+
+    with patch.object(cuda.logger, "warning_once") as warn:
+        cuda._warn_if_slow_pre_sm80_backend(backend, capability)
+    warn.assert_not_called()

@@ -181,6 +181,34 @@ def _get_backend_priorities(
             ]
 
 
+# Triton-based backends whose tl.dot lowering does not use tensor cores on
+# pre-SM80 GPUs with current Triton, see
+# https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60821.
+_SLOW_PRE_SM80_BACKENDS = (
+    AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN,
+    AttentionBackendEnum.FLEX_ATTENTION,
+)
+
+
+def _warn_if_slow_pre_sm80_backend(
+    backend: AttentionBackendEnum, device_capability: DeviceCapability
+) -> None:
+    """Warn once when auto-selection lands on a slow path on pre-SM80 GPUs."""
+    if device_capability >= DeviceCapability(8, 0):
+        return
+    if backend not in _SLOW_PRE_SM80_BACKENDS:
+        return
+    logger.warning_once(
+        "Using the %s attention backend on a GPU with compute capability "
+        "%d.%d (pre-SM80, e.g. Turing/T4). On these GPUs the Triton attention "
+        "kernels do not use tensor cores, so prefill can be much slower than "
+        "on SM80+ GPUs. See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60821.",
+        backend.name,
+        device_capability.major,
+        device_capability.minor,
+    )
+
+
 def _backend_cls_path(backend_cls: type[AttentionBackend]) -> str:
     module, qualname = backend_cls.full_cls_name()
     return f"{module}.{qualname}"
@@ -505,6 +533,8 @@ def get_attn_backend_cls(
                     selected_backend.name,
                 )
 
+        _warn_if_slow_pre_sm80_backend(selected_backend, device_capability)
+
         logger.info_once(
             "Using %s attention backend out of potential backends: %s.",
             selected_backend.name,
